**Additional Information**  
  
**WORK CONDITIONS**  
Exposure to:

* Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks
* In-store temperatures range from 32 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas
* Extreme weather conditions including
  + temperatures ranging from 0 degrees up to 110 degrees outside
  + Rain, fog, sleet, snow, ice, wind, dust, and more
* Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside
* Fumes from food odors
* Exposure to cornmeal dust
* Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler
* Hot surfaces/tools from oven and hot plates up to 500 degrees or higher
* Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts

**SENSING** :

* Talking and listening on telephone
* Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks
* Depth perception
* Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

  
**TEMPERAMENTS** :

* The ability to direct activities
* Perform repetitive tasks
* Work alone and with others
* Work adequately under stress
* Meet strict quality control standards
* Work well with others
* Satisfy unhappy customers
* Analyze and compile data
* Make judgments and decisions
* Problem Solving

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Standing
  + Most tasks are performed from a standing position
  + Height of most work surfaces is between 36 and 48 inches
* Walking/Jogging/Running
  + For short distances or for short durations
* Sitting
  + Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table
* Lifting
  + Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck
  + Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'
  + Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72” high
* Carrying
  + Large bags/boxes/crates, weighing up to 50 pounds, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves
  + Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray
* Pushing
  + To move trays which are usually placed on dollies
  + A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24 - 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push
* Climbing
  + Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance
* Stooping/Bending
  + Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station
  + Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station
  + Duration of this position is approximately 45 - 120 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day
  + Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients
* Crouching/Squatting
  + Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas
* Reaching
  + Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward
  + Workers reach above 72” occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves
  + Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes
  + Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones
* Hand Tasks
  + Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day
  + Frequently, activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists
  + Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter
  + Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes
  + Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes
  + Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

**Crouching/Squatting**

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

**Reaching**

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

**Driving**

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Agency Description
  
  
The Department of Small Business Services (SBS) is a dynamic, client-centered Agency whose mission is to serve New York’s small businesses and commercial districts. SBS makes it easier for companies in New York City to form, do business, and grow by providing direct assistance to business owners, promoting commercial districts, promoting financial and economic opportunity among minority and women-owned businesses, preparing New Yorkers for jobs, and linking employers with a skilled and qualified workforce.  
  
  
  
Division Description
  
  
The Division of Citywide Workforce Opportunity (CWO) at the NYC Department of Small Business Services (SBS) serves over 100,000 jobseekers and 1000 employers each year through its employment and training programs. Specifically, CWO oversees a network of 18 Workforce1 (WF1) Career Centers, operated in all five boroughs, and a broad and diverse training portfolio including individual training grants for over a dozen occupations and more than two dozen cohort-based occupational training programs, in such areas as technology, health care, transportation, construction, media and entertainment, and food and beverage sectors, that are offered in collaboration with higher education institutions and non-profit training providers.  
  
  
  
The Industry Engagement team within CWO serves to directly engage employers into the Workforce1 Career Centers and training programs, as well as to build the capacity of the system to more effectively engage employers. Reporting to the Deputy Commissioner for Citywide Workforce Opportunity, the Managing Director leads CWO’s labor market intelligence, employer engagement, business development, and related capacity building functions. This includes analyzing the workforce needs of NYC’s industries and employers; making a compelling case to NYC employers to utilize the Workforce1 system for their recruitment needs; connecting employers to workforce solutions through Workforce1 Career Centers, Training, and Jobs NYC; building the capacity of the public workforce system to respond to labor market demand and to effectively engage employers; and ensuring that employers’ interactions with all facets of the Workforce1 system are characterized by exceptional customer service. Working collaboratively with CWO leadership, Workforce1 Career Centers, training providers, and other relevant stakeholders, the Managing Director expands access to good jobs for unemployed and underemployed New Yorkers while ensuring that the public workforce system for adults remains aligned with current and future labor market needs.
  
  
Responsibilities include the following areas:
  
  
Labor Market Analysis:
  
  

* Lead CWO’s labor market intelligence strategy, translating economic and workforce trends into actionable priorities for employer engagement, training investments, and service delivery, with an eye towards opportunities for unemployed and underemployed New Yorkers from disadvantaged communities, and alignment with the City’s economic development goals.

  

* Analyze existing data sets from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Community Survey, New York State Department of Labor, and tools such as Lightcast and LinkedIn; survey existing research and publications on workforce challenges and shortages; mine internal data on program performance; and engage industry associations and employers for feedback through roundtables, focus groups, and individual conversations.

  

* Share labor market insights on industry trends, occupational demand, wages, skills gaps and emerging workforce needs with Workforce1 Career Centers and training providers in easily digestible and actionable formats.

  
Employer Engagement and Strategy:
  
  

* Develop strategies in collaboration with the Workforce1 Career Centers and training providers to leverage the assets and capacity of the public workforce system to solve pressing hiring and workforce challenges for NYC’s business community.

  

* Expand and diversify the businesses that utilize Workforce1 to meet their hiring needs. Effectively communicate Workforce1’s value to different sectors of the economy and build brand recognition with employers not yet connected to the system.

  

* Develop and incubate partnerships with strategically identified employer partners that offer high value opportunities for unemployed and underemployed New Yorkers at scale.

  

* Serve as a senior representative of CWO with employers, industry associations, labor organizations, business intermediaries, and economic development partners, building partnerships that inform workforce strategy and create employment opportunities at scale.

  

* Involve employers in training program identification and design; work-based learning such as internships and apprenticeships; and direct hiring pipelines.

  

* Track and monitor employment outcomes and customer satisfaction, identify gaps and opportunities for improvement, and collaborate with divisional and vendor leadership to enhance and shift strategies over time.

  
Capacity Building:
  
  

* Build the capacity of the public workforce system to follow industry trends, assess employer needs, engage new employers, and retain and expand existing employer partnerships. This includes capacity-building for staff within the CWO division as well as our Workforce1, training vendor, and community partner organizations, including regular meetings with account managers, recruiters, and career development staff, and opportunities for professional development and participation in industry events.

  

* Strengthen feedback loops between employers and provider organizations to ensure training and service design is updated over time for optimal results.

  

* Identify tools and create processes that help the system build industry expertise and stay up to date on shifts in demand over time.

  

* Leverage technology to support providers in identifying employers, tracking employer engagement, sharing equitably across the system, and facilitating the placement validation process.

  

* Develop communications materials to assist account managers in selling recruitment services.

  

* Supervise and mentor the industry engagement team.

  

* Foster a culture of exceptional customer service for job-seekers and employers, in which customers feel valued and heard, and a culture of trusted partnership with vendors, industry associations, and community partners, prioritizing transparency, collaboration, follow-through, and results.

  

* Serve as a member of CWO’s senior leadership team, working collaboratively with other senior leaders of the division to drive strategy, collaboration and performance.

  

* Support special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

  
  
Minimum Qualifications Requirements
  
  
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college and at least 5 years of combined full-time experience in any of the following: leading or managing in-house business development and sales/marketing activities; providing external business development, sales/marketing, strategic planning, or management consulting services to employer clients; serving in a leadership role at a trade/professional association, BID, economic development organization, or similar group; or related experience.

**Head of Engineering Job Description:** Scope, Impact & Qualifications Reports to: CEO Level: Executive (CTO-equivalent scope) Org size: ~25 engineers Time split: 70% Product / 30% Discipline ROLE SUMMARY The Head of Engineering owns the technical outcomes of Maestro's entire product suite while also serving as the top of the engineering discipline ladder: every engineering manager and individual contributor ultimately ladders up to this role. The position deliberately splits attention: 70% product execution, 30% discipline accountability. Product delivery is the immediate, ongoing accountability; discipline work compounds over time and requires protected but smaller blocks of focus so it doesn't get crowded out by delivery pressure. This role sits at the center of Maestro's matrix structure, accountable for craft quality and standards company-wide, while ensuring embedded engineering talent on each product team is pointed at the right priorities.
  
  
**SCOPE • Org reach:** all engineering leads across all product lines report into this role (directly or via a lead layer), the senior-most engineering accountability in the company. • Product surface: full product suite, every active product line's engineering output. • Discipline surface: engineering-wide standards, tooling, and process, independent of which product team an engineer sits on. THE 70%: PRODUCT ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering is the single accountable owner for engineering execution across Maestro's product portfolio.
  
  
**What this looks like day to day:** • Partners with the engineering leads of every product line to ensure their teams are resourced against the right priorities: not just busy, but correctly sequenced. • Accountable for ensuring product strategy and roadmap direction are translated into clear, actionable engineering plans, serving as the connective layer between Product and Delivery leadership and the engineering organization, primarily through engineering leads embedded within product teams. • Accountable for applying technical judgment to turn high-level strategic priorities into concrete technical execution plans, enabling and guiding engineering leads to scope, sequence, and de-risk delivery across their product areas. • Identifies where product priorities and engineering capacity are misaligned across teams and resolves the tradeoff, including cross-team resourcing calls.
  
  

* Is the escalation point when a product line's engineering execution is off track, and is accountable for getting it back on track. Impact: Every product line ships against strategy, not just against what's easiest to build. Product and Delivery leaders have one accountable engineering partner instead of negotiating separately with each product line's lead. THE 30%: DISCIPLINE ACCOUNTABILITY The Head of Engineering owns what "good engineering" means at Maestro, independent of the product line.

**What this looks like day to day:** • Sets and maintains company-wide engineering standards (code quality, architecture principles, technical debt posture). • Owns cross-cutting technical initiatives that no single product team should solve independently, e.g. product suite services and universal QA automation. • Defines how AI tooling is used across engineering, including guardrails to ensure AI usage improves output quality and velocity rather than introducing risk or degrading craft.
  
  

* Identifies and removes friction in how engineering work gets done company-wide, streamlining processes that slow every team down in the same way. • Is the ultimate accountable owner for engineering management practice (how EMs lead, how performance is evaluated, how the craft is grown) even where day-to-day people management is embedded in product teams. Impact: Engineering quality, velocity, and management practice don't fragment by product line. An engineer's experience of "how we build software here" is consistent no matter which team they're on, and the org gets the benefits of scale (shared tooling, shared standards) instead of each team reinventing its own.

SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE • Engineers across the organization deliver flawless technical execution that earns long-term client retention and supports growth. • Product lines are resourced against strategic priority, with tradeoffs made explicitly rather than by default. • Engineering leads across product lines operate with a shared technical bar and shared tooling. • Company-wide initiatives (QA automation, AI usage standards) ship and get adopted, not just get designed.
  
  

* Engineering management practice is consistent and healthy across the org, even though EMs are embedded in product teams day to day. QUALIFICATIONS Maestro hires for demonstrated capability, not years-of-service checkboxes. The bar below is competency-based: what someone needs to be able to do, not how long they've been doing it. Required competencies: • Has personally carried end-to-end accountability for engineering delivery across more than one product or team simultaneously: not just led a single team, but balanced competing priorities across several.
* Can translate ambiguous, high-level strategy (from product, business, or leadership) into a technical execution plan that engineers can actually build against, without needing someone else to do that translation. • Has designed or materially improved an engineering standard, process, or tooling investment that worked across teams (not a single-team fix) and can point to the before/after. • Comfortably operates in a matrixed environment, influencing and aligning engineering leads, their teams, and cross-functional stakeholders without relying on formal authority. • Has hands-on technical depth sufficient to earn credibility with senior engineers and to personally evaluate technical tradeoffs.

This is not a purely managerial role. • Has direct experience managing or mentoring engineering managers, not only individual contributors. • Demonstrates sound judgment on when to standardize company-wide versus when to let product teams operate with autonomy. Strongly preferred: • Experience operating at this scope inside a company of comparable size (roughly 15 to 50 engineers), where formal process is lighter and judgment calls happen more often than policy lookups.
  
  

* Direct experience setting a company's approach to AI-assisted engineering (tooling choices, guardrails, or usage standards) rather than just using AI tools personally. • A track record of building or scaling QA automation, testing strategy, or release process across multiple teams. • Experience partnering directly with Product and Delivery leadership as a peer, not just receiving requirements from them. • Experience leading engineering for always-on, customer-facing digital products or live-service platforms, where availability, release discipline, observability, incident response, and rapid cross-functional coordination directly affect the end-user experience and client retention.

**What we're explicitly not requiring:** • A specific prior title (VP Engineering, CTO, etc.). We care about scope actually carried, not the title it came with. • A minimum years-of-experience threshold. Competency and evidence of impact matter more than tenure.
  
  

* Deep expertise in every technology in Maestro's stack. Technical judgment and the ability to evaluate tradeoffs matter more than hands-on fluency in any one language or framework.

**Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR) Overview:**
  
Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR) seeks to deliver effective independent risk management of the activities and processes associated with managing the Company’s capital, liquidity and interest rate risks, including price risk in the CFO managed securities portfolio. As the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) function covering the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Group, we also bring together a holistic point of view across all seven risk types for the Company’s CFO.
  
  
The team helps Bank of America grow responsibly through developing our teammates, promoting opportunity and an inclusive culture, and approaching our work with intellectual curiosity. EFR delivers its mission through a steadfast commitment to its values: cultivating diversity of thought and valuing different perspectives and experiences; promoting learning, fostering relationships and creativity; and developing talent, advancing careers, and creating leaders within Global Risk Management and across the company. Our goal is to ensure that a healthy and sustainable liquidity, capital, and interest rate risk (IRR) profile is maintained through baseline economic scenarios, as well as during times of market and idiosyncratic stress.

  
  

**EFR Division: Liquidity Risk Management**

Enterprise Liquidity Risk Management is a department within Enterprise Financial Risk (EFR). This group is responsible for providing an independent assessment of Bank of America’s Liquidity risk, as described within BAC’s Risk Framework. The goal of the department is that a healthy and sustainable Liquidity profile is maintained through a business as usual environment and also during times of stress to support our ability to meet our financial obligations.

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with entrepreneurial, action- and results-oriented professionals. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and helping them reach their potential. A&M is different by design: we give people ownership and impact from day one, fuel development through real opportunity, and provide direct access to leaders who invest in our growth. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact clients and shape our industry. Guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity, our collaborative, globally minded environment is why our people love working at A&M.

**The Team**  
The Healthcare Industry Group, a subsidiary of A&M, leads transformational change in healthcare. As established leaders and trusted advisors, we deliver results for healthcare executives, boards, private equity firms, investors, law firms, and government agencies. Our team brings diverse perspectives and experiences to assist clients with enhancing financial and operational performance, accelerating strategic growth, and optimizing value throughout the investment lifecycle.

We provide specialized services in interim management, restructuring, revenue cycle management, M&A, compliance, digital technology, and analytics. Our professionals collaborate with a wide range of organizations, including health systems, physician groups, medical schools, behavioral health institutes, managed care organizations, healthcare investors, medical device companies, and suppliers, as well as vision centers, dental practices, and laboratories.

As a Director you will be leading a team and acting as the main conduit between healthcare clients and our team on a range of complex assignments. You will manage projects by overseeing interview activities, gathering relevant data, developing goals and deadlines, reviewing work product of junior staff, and communicating with clients directly. Depending on the client project the responsibilities of a director may typically include:

* Engaging with clients to foster trust, credibility, and compatible relationships.
* Assessing how clients are approaching their businesses. Engaging in c-suite and board-level conversations regarding the challenges facing them and strategic initiatives for solving them.
* Swiftly Assessing business needs and designing and implementing measurable solutions that span all aspects of revenue cycle operations.
* Communicating regularly with clients and project team members, escalating any matters that require additional attention and consideration from engagement leadership.
* Providing guidance to manage a client through crisis.
* Collaborating and aligning with representatives from other service lines.
* Effectively managing client project plans, including defining, prioritizing, and sequencing work to meet deadlines and manage on time deliverables.
* Managing performance of project teams, including assigning and delegating project responsibilities and providing on-the-job coaching and constructive feedback. Mentoring junior staff.
* Improving client tracking tools and developing KPIs and metrics to identify and quantify operational performance improvement opportunities for one-time cash acceleration and recurring income statement benefit.
* Redesigning and implementing leading practice workflows, addressing deficits in quality, and driving operational and financial outcomes across different levels of healthcare organizations.
* Knowledge of engagement economics and overall product delivery, budgeting, and timely billing & collections including managing the implementation risk and profitability for smaller scale projects.
* Developing and delivering high-quality work products, utilizing both qualitative and quantitative data, including cash waterfalls, payment velocity, cost-to-collect, and others.
* Utilizing experience and expertise to effectively function in interim roles (e.g., VP Revenue Cycle, other).
* Developing clear transition and handing off plans to ensure improvements are sustainable.
* Building relationships with clients and seeking opportunities to expand the scope of business while generating leads. Acting as an integral member of the sales team, developing significant portions of proposal and pitch documents.

We are seeking someone to join our team with an entrepreneurial and collaborative mindset who will manage ambiguity and thrive in a fast-paced environment. You will use your judgment to assign and delegate project responsibilities while balancing the need for efficiency and providing on-the-job training opportunities to further develop staff skillsets.

Revenue cycle projects may include, but are not limited to: due diligences, performance assessments, enterprise performance improvement, full-scale implementations, and interim management for a broad range of healthcare providers and supporting services companies.

We are not your typical consulting firm. We are entrepreneurial, action-oriented, and results-driven professionals who take a hands-on approach to solving our clients’ problems and helping them drive value and growth. We are nimble, resourceful, proactive, can pivot to adapt quickly, when needed, and develop plans that drive real results. You will be part of a team that is passionate about delivering transformational change and making an impact in the healthcare industry.

Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.  
  
The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down.
  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production.
  
  
Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo.
* Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected.
* Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts.
* Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view.
* Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks.
* Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics.
* Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform.
* Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes.
* Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage.
* Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support.
* Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software.

  
A day in the life  
You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all.  
  
About the team  
The Leo NOC and LIM Operations Tooling team builds the operational products that keep a global space and terrestrial telecom network healthy and its operations efficient. We sit next to the people who use our tools, the Network Operations Center and the Incident Management Team. We measure success by how much faster, quieter, and more automated operations become as the network scales toward and beyond general availability.

The Frontline Services Technician I is a technical role responsible for providing professional end-user support, monitoring IT infrastructure, resolving routine incidents, and escalating complex or high-risk issues.

The role operates primarily through established procedures, knowledge articles, runbooks, and escalation processes.

**Essential Functions**

* Provide technical support for end users, applications, endpoints, network connectivity, and common IT services, resolving routine issues using established troubleshooting procedures, knowledge articles, and runbooks.

**End User Support Focus**

Grafana Cloud moves millions of metrics, log lines, and traces per second from our customers' environments into a highly available, low-latency stack that processes and stores this data, and serves it to dashboards and alerting tools. Position Summary
  
  
The Senior Program Manager, Network Build leads the delivery of fiber network construction across one or more markets and the Design Areas within them. This role owns the plan for each market from an accepted design package through an operational network, and is accountable for keeping every Design Area moving through the same sixteen milestones, from package accepted to operational. The Senior Program Manager sets the standard for how the Network Build Program Managers plan, report and escalate, and is the primary voice of the build program to senior leaders. The role also helps build and refine the processes the team runs on, so that planning, handoffs, reporting and vendor payment become more consistent and more efficient as the program grows.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
**Plan and schedule ownership**

* Own the schedule and plan logic for assigned markets, including dependencies, crew capacity, quantities, production rates and weather effects, and keep them accurate as work moves from Project Controls to the Network Build team.
* Maintain the sixteen-milestone plan for every Design Area, and decide when a milestone is complete using evidence from the responsible team rather than assumption.
* Re-forecast dates when crew counts, weather, permits or materials change, and explain the effect on the market finish date.

**Milestone management and handoffs**

* Confirm the Operational state of each Design Area. The Senior Program Manager and the Network Build Program Managers confirm it; no other team does.
* Manage the release of each project to construction, including the handoff to Supply Chain for materials staging and the notice to Sales and Marketing.
* In Prescott, run the pre-construction approval sequence: Construction completes the utility locates and reports to the Program Manager, the Program Manager schedules the pre-construction walks, Design and Engineering makes comments and corrections, the City approves, and Construction is then released.

**Cross-functional leadership**

* Coordinate Design and Engineering, the Permit Specialist, Supply Chain, Construction, Sales and Marketing and the Network Operations Center so that each handoff is clean and dated.
* Hold a weekly meeting with each team on Thursday or Friday, collect final updates by Monday, and prepare the reports for the Wednesday 30-60-90 day review.
* Escalate risks, delays and decisions early, with a recommendation and the effect on schedule and cost.

**Vendor and financial oversight**

* Make sure construction vendors are paid accurately and on time by reviewing each submitted invoice against the approved design prints before it is entered for payment.
* Track budget against forecast for each Design Area and flag variances to leadership.

**Reporting and governance**

* Report status using four labels: On Track, At-Risk, Off-Track and Complete.
* Track grant-funded markets against their commitments and prepare the reporting those programs require.
* Review the plan data for accuracy each week, and correct gaps before reports are issued.
* Communicate directly with executives and senior leaders in writing and in meetings, presenting status, risks, decisions and recommendations in plain language with the conclusion first.

**Team leadership**

* Coach and review the work of the Network Build Program Managers, set consistent reporting standards, and step in on the most complex or at-risk markets.

**Process development and improvement**

* Help design and document the processes the Network Build team follows, including milestone definitions, handoffs between teams, schedule updates, reporting and vendor invoice review.
* Review how the processes work in practice each quarter, identify recurring delays, rework and gaps, and recommend and lead improvements.
* Turn lessons from completed Design Areas into updated standards, templates and checklists that every Network Build Program Manager uses.
* Work with Design and Engineering, Permitting, Supply Chain, Construction, Sales and Marketing and the Network Operations Center to agree on process changes before they are adopted.
* Train and coach the Network Build Program Managers on new and revised processes, and confirm that they are followed.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* A bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* At least eight years of program or project management experience, including at least five years delivering outside plant fiber, utility or telecommunications construction.
* Demonstrated ability to manage schedules with dependencies, crew capacity and weather, and to explain a forecast change in plain language.
* Experience managing construction vendors, including invoice review against design documents.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing and presenting executive-level status reports, briefings and recommendations that are clear, accurate and concise.

**Preferred**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
* Experience with federal or state broadband grant programs.
* Experience with permitting for rights-of-way, railroad, highway and utility pole attachments.

What Success Looks Like
  
  

* Every Design Area in the assigned markets shows an accurate, current date for each milestone.

* Vendor invoices are verified against the design prints and paid without rework.

**About Us**

Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: acquisition, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.

We've found product-market fit (multi-million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health) and we're backed by top-tier VCs with years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future.

As a Senior Technical Account Manager (Senior TAM, L6) at Affirm, you will own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, delivering against SLAs, fielding technical inquiries, and performing investigations and analysis, while also driving technical initiatives that translate merchant business objectives into technical strategies and product optimizations. Senior TAMs are part of the Engineering team and collaborate closely with Affirm's Product, Engineering, Operations, Customer Success, and Frontline Technical Support teams.
  
  
This is an operations-heavy role to start. Expect the majority of your early focus to be on keeping merchant integrations healthy—monitoring, triage, troubleshooting, and SLA delivery—while you progressively take on more custom solutioning and cross-functional initiatives. Over your first 6–12 months, as you build operational mastery, you will grow into owning your own book of accounts and carrying it through to end-to-end account ownership.
  
  
A Senior TAM independently owns operational health across the strategic alliance portfolio, designs custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations, drives cross-team collaboration on initiatives, acts as a technical lead on team projects, and mentors less-experienced members of the team.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Own the operational aspect of technical account management across Affirm's strategic alliance portfolio—alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and fielding technical inquiries—so integrations stay healthy and issues are resolved quickly.
* Deliver against SLAs, proactively surfacing technical risks before they become customer-impacting and responding with urgency to merchant issues.
* Perform in-depth investigations and root-cause analysis across logs, queries, and integration data, owning resolution end to end and escalating to cross-functional partners or executives when needed.
* Drive technical initiatives and partner with internal and merchant stakeholders on launch initiatives—expansions, promotions, new product adoption, and integration optimizations—that grow the value of the accounts after launch.
* Design and deliver high-scope, often-custom integration solutions grounded in Affirm's standard integrations—combining, extending, and tailoring them to complex, open-ended problems while balancing speed, quality, maintainability, reliability, and scalability.
* Act as a technical lead for internal projects, defining and delivering well-scoped milestones and executing the project roadmap.
* Operationalize best practices by creating and updating playbooks, runbooks, alerting, and UAT certification plans across the strategic alliance portfolio and continuously reduce keep-the-lights-on (KTLO) work.
* Partner with Product and Engineering leads to identify, plan, and prioritize projects based on team goals and resources, acting as the voice of the merchant to influence the roadmap.
* Mentor and level up less-experienced TAMs, share learnings from your integrations and investigations, and contribute to interviewing and team development.
* Over your first 6–12 months, grow into owning a dedicated book of strategic alliance accounts—carrying operational ownership through to end-to-end account ownership.

What We Look For
  
  

* Professional Background: at least six years in a technical, external-facing role such as Technical Account Management, Solutions/Partner Engineering, or Solutions Architecture—ideally within FinTech, payments, or SaaS—with a demonstrated track record of owning the operational health of technical accounts and delivering against SLAs.
* Operational Ownership: proven ability to run alerting, monitoring, troubleshooting, and technical inquiries across a set of accounts, balancing reactive operational work with proactive initiatives.
* Ownership & Autonomy: proven ability to independently scope and deliver complex, open-ended technical work, and to partner with stakeholders on launch initiatives, with strong project management and follow-through.
* API Expertise: deep understanding of RESTful APIs, webhooks, and the HTTP protocol, with hands-on experience using tools like Postman to debug and validate integrations.
* Architecture Fluency: Experience in API integrations and the ability to design custom solutions on top of them to solve complex merchant challenges.
* Coding & Code Fluency: ability to read and understand production-level code (HTML, JavaScript, SQL, and ideally one server-side language such as Python) and to author new, novel queries to diagnose merchant or system issues.
* Troubleshooting Acumen: ability to diagnose issues using browser developer consoles, log analysis and observability platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Chronosphere), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira, Notion).
* Technical Communication: excellent verbal and written communication; able to tailor explanations to both non-technical leaders and technical teams, read a room and adjust in real time, and synthesize technical challenges back to internal teams.
* Relationship Management: ability to discover and develop relationships with technical decision-makers, secure written consensus on integration milestones, and drive cross-team collaboration.
* Leadership & Mentorship: demonstrated ability to mentor teammates, set best practices, and lead technical initiatives; a growth mindset with self-awareness and a habit of seeking and acting on feedback.

Nice to Have
  
  

* Familiarity with the payments ecosystem.
* Familiarity with web/mobile application architecture.
* Experience implementing or customizing e-commerce platforms, payment gateways, or in-store point-of-sale systems.
* Experience acting as a technical lead on cross-functional projects and influencing product roadmaps.

* Establish clear accountability for delivery performance across practices, business lines, and service portfolios.
* Create a culture of operational excellence, customer focus, transparency, urgency, and disciplined execution.

**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, spanning three brands: LawnStarter, Lawn Love, and Home Gnome. We've cleared $750M in bookings and turned a profit three years running. Founded in Austin in 2013, we're a team of about 180 that scales past 500 employees during peak season. The marketplace itself is easy to describe and hard to run well: a customer requests a service, we price the job and match it to an eligible Pro, the Pro claims and completes the work, and we process payment and take a commission.

We're entering the most ambitious stretch in the company's history as we build new verticals, new software products, and the groundwork to become a multi-billion-dollar company.

One of our company values is AI or Extinction: every task, AI-first. No exceptions, no excuses. Top 1% or we're already a fossil. This role is hired against that bar.

**The Role**

This is a biz ops generalist role, built for someone who wants to work across many parts of the business instead of owning one narrow lane. You'll start as an individual contributor with no direct reports, in a new seat reporting directly to the COO. Your first owned area will be building Service Delivery into a working operational function. This will entail adding structure, visibility and process to the way we ensure as many customer jobs as possible are completed successfully and on time by LawnStarter Pros, in lawn care and other services we offer now and over time.

New projects will show up unscoped over time. That's by design. As LawnStarter enters new verticals and grows toward a multi-billion-dollar future, big problems will keep surfacing with no obvious owner, and you'll be one of the people the COO trusts to run them down.

**What makes this role different:**

* You work on some of the biggest company-wide projects, cutting across teams and functional areas.
* You'll be a top builder in Brain, LawnStarter's internal AI toolkit built on Claude Code that already powers everything we do across the company: metric queries, document drafting, bug triage, and more. We expect you to approach your work in an AI-first fashion, leveraging Brain to build new systems and processes that will push the limits of how fast AI can accelerate business results. Every project you run is built AI-first: the analysis, the tooling, the process automation, the monitoring. You build it yourself instead of waiting on an analyst or engineer.
* You own outcomes end to end, from recommendation through execution. Strategy without follow-through doesn't count here.

**What You'll Own**

* **Service Delivery, from the ground up.** Despite LawnStarter's considerable scale and reach, Service Delivery doesn't exist yet as a dedicated function. You'll help define the standards we should meet for job completion rates and speed, measure whether we hit them, and design processes, incentives and real-time interventions that get tested with Pros and customers in the field to lift performance. Scope covers every vertical and every delivery model, from today's 1099 Pros to potential W-2 crews under future evaluation.
* **Raising customer & Pro retention rates.** When we deliver service with excellence, Pros and customers alike stay with us longer. Working tightly with peers across Product, Data and Support, you'll identify new opportunities for us to boost retention and LTV and play a key role in driving resulting initiatives cross-functionally.
* **Whatever comes next.** New projects will land on your plate as the company grows into new verticals and builds new software products. You'll take them from "we should look into this" to building and then running systems with structure, KPIs and owners.

**Problems to Solve**

**Build a Service Delivery function that doesn't exist yet.** Right now, no one formally owns whether LawnStarter delivers the service it promises. You'll define the standard for what a Pro should deliver, then build the agents and pipelines that measure adherence to it and run the tests that change behaviors and outcomes in the field.

**Move metrics.** Leverage systems thinking and AI expertise to drive business results that sit across various functional teams. That means untangling handoffs where several teams touch a problem or goal and no one team owns the outcome.

**Take unscoped problems from ideas to fully-running and automated systems.** Some of the most important work here hasn't been named yet. At some point, someone will raise a fuzzy, unframed problem and say it needs attention. Your job is to take that starting point and build whatever tooling or process it needs, at record speed, and hand back something that runs, with a clear owner and quantitative targets attached.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

* Service Delivery is a working function with a defined (and elevated) service standard, a way to measure adherence to it, clear SOPs, and an intervention and incentive playbook that's been tested and proven to lift results.
* At least one project nobody had scoped a year earlier has gone from "we should look into this" to a heavily-automated, running system with a named owner and tracked KPIs.
* Tools you built with AI are in daily use by people other than you, and the way you work has raised the bar for how the company uses AI.
* The COO can hand you a gray-area problem with no playbook and trust that what comes back is data, a recommendation, and a plan to execute it.

  
**Requirements**

**Who You Are**

Overview:

The Manager, 2LOD KYC Quality Assurance & Program Enhancement will play a key role in building and maturing the Bank’s second-line KYC oversight function, with responsibility for helping design the program, establish the quality assurance and testing framework, and build and develop a team to support KYC testing, quality assurance, risk evaluation, and ongoing program monitoring.

The role will focus primarily on Know Your Customer (KYC), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), with broader coverage across the BSA/AML lifecycle, including transaction monitoring, investigations and SAR processes, and OFAC/Sanctions.

A key objective of the role is to evaluate whether the Bank develops an appropriate and complete understanding of its customers through KYC/CDD/EDD and whether that customer knowledge is effectively incorporated into ongoing monitoring, investigations, escalation, and risk decisioning.

The Manager will identify control gaps, process inefficiencies, inconsistent application of standards, and opportunities to better connect BSA/AML activities across the customer lifecycle. Through testing, quality assurance, thematic reviews, risk assessments, and root-cause analysis, the role will translate findings into sustainable enhancements to processes, controls, policies, procedures, standards, training, and systems.

The Manager will also work closely with data and analytics resources to develop meaningful Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), establish management reporting, identify emerging risk and quality trends, and communicate results and actionable insights to business line leadership, BSA/AML leadership, governance committees, and executive management.

Responsibilities:

**Second-Line KYC Program Development & Leadership**

* Help design, build, and mature the Bank’s second-line KYC oversight function, including program governance, testing methodology, risk-based coverage, quality standards, reporting, and escalation frameworks.
* Develop a risk-based testing and QA approach for assessing the effectiveness of KYC/CDD/EDD processes and controls.
* Build and lead a team responsible for KYC testing, quality assurance, thematic reviews, risk evaluation, and program monitoring.
* Establish consistent testing methodologies, documentation standards, sampling approaches, issue-rating criteria, and reporting protocols.
* Develop a scalable program that evolves based on changes in customer risk, business activities, regulatory expectations, testing results, and emerging risk trends.
* Provide effective second-line challenge and oversight while partnering constructively with first-line KYC and business functions to drive sustainable improvement.

**KYC/CDD/EDD Quality Assurance & Risk Evaluation**

* Lead risk-based QA and testing across KYC, CDD, and EDD, evaluating the quality, completeness, consistency, and effectiveness of customer risk assessments, documentation, escalation, and decisioning.
* Assess adherence to BSA/AML policies, procedures, customer risk-rating methodologies, due diligence requirements, and established review standards.
* Evaluate whether higher-risk customers receive appropriate levels of due diligence and whether material customer risks are sufficiently identified, investigated, documented, and escalated.
* Assess consistency in how KYC requirements and risk-based judgment are applied across business lines, customer segments, reviewers, and approval channels.
* Conduct targeted and thematic reviews to identify systemic weaknesses, emerging risks, control gaps, and areas requiring deeper assessment.
* Evaluate whether KYC controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively and identify opportunities to strengthen the overall control environment.

**Connecting KYC Across the BSA/AML Lifecycle**

* Expand testing and thematic coverage across transaction monitoring, FIU investigations, SAR processes, and OFAC/Sanctions to evaluate the effectiveness and consistency of customer risk management across BSA functions.
* Assess whether information developed through KYC/CDD/EDD, including expected activity, business purpose, ownership structure, geography, products, counterparties, and known risk factors, is effectively incorporated into downstream monitoring and investigations.
* Evaluate whether investigations appropriately consider the Bank’s broader knowledge of the customer rather than reviewing transactional activity in isolation.
* Assess whether material information identified through transaction monitoring, investigations, SAR-related activities, EDD, or sanctions reviews is appropriately fed back into the customer’s risk profile and ongoing due diligence.
* Identify ineffective handoffs, information gaps, inconsistent decisions, and duplicative reviews across BSA functions.
* Recommend opportunities to better integrate KYC, ongoing due diligence, transaction monitoring, investigations, sanctions, and customer risk management into a more cohesive end-to-end framework.

**Process Optimization & Program Enhancement**

* Conduct end-to-end and thematic reviews to identify control gaps, inconsistent decisioning, process inefficiencies, duplicative activities, ineffective handoffs, and opportunities for process optimization.
* Perform root-cause analysis to distinguish individual execution errors from systemic issues involving policies, procedures, standards, training, technology, data, workflow design, or organizational handoffs.
* Identify opportunities to streamline processes, reduce unnecessary rework, improve information sharing, and strengthen the overall quality and effectiveness of KYC and BSA/AML reviews.
* Translate testing and QA results into actionable recommendations for enhancements to policies, procedures, standards, controls, training, workflows, and technology.
* Establish and support calibration activities to promote consistent interpretation and application of KYC requirements and risk-based decisioning.
* Partner with relevant stakeholders to monitor remediation and assess whether corrective actions result in sustained improvements.

**KPI/KRI, Analytics & Executive Risk Reporting**

* Partner closely with data analysts and analytics resources to develop the data capabilities, metrics, and reporting necessary to evaluate KYC risk and program effectiveness.
* Develop and maintain meaningful KPIs and KRIs covering areas such as KYC quality, policy adherence, customer risk-rating accuracy, review timeliness, exception trends, decision consistency, higher-risk populations, process effectiveness, and control performance.
* Establish thresholds and trend indicators to identify deterioration in quality, emerging risk, changing risk concentrations, or areas requiring management attention.
* Integrate testing results, QA findings, risk assessments, and business data to identify risk trends, recurring themes, systemic weaknesses, and emerging areas of concern.
* Develop dashboards and management reporting that translate complex KYC data and testing results into clear and actionable risk insights.

UNMAS also works closely with the Syrian Government which has designated the Ministry of Emergency and Disaster Management (MoEDM) as the national focal point for mine action. ### **Job Specific Context**

Background: UNMAS Syria Programme

Operating under the mandate of Security Council resolution 2165 (renewed in 2017 with SCR 2393), UNMAS deployed to Syria at the request of the Deputy Regional Humanitarian Coordinator in August 2015 and subsequently activated the Mine Action Sub Sector under the Protection Sector to address the impact of explosive hazards within Syria. UNMAS acted as the lead agency for the Mine Action Sub sector for Syria. Established in Damascus since 2018, following the signature of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Syrian Arab Republic, UNMAS strives to expand humanitarian mine action in Syria, with the aim of responding to high humanitarian needs. This includes humanitarian mine action activities prioritized in the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for Syria: risk education, victim assistance, survey and clearance.

The conflict in Syria has been characterized by the extensive use of explosive weapons, which resulted in large-scale explosive hazard contamination, with the presence of diversified types of ordnances. According to the Syrian Arab Republic Humanitarian Needs Response Plan(HNRP) 2026, over 14.3 million Syrians are estimated to be at risk of explosive ordnance (EO) contamination; men, women, and children are exposed to the threat of grave injuries and death on a daily basis.

Mitigating EO risks and supporting survivors are a key priority given the scale of EO contamination with 2335 civilian casualties recorded between December 2024 and June 2026.

UNMAS play a central role in reducing harm through non-technical survey, EO disposal and clearance, inclusive risk education integrated with critical services such as education, agriculture, and cash/livelihoods, and sensitive community engagement, while facilitating referrals to survey and clearance actors where feasible.

* Interest and knowledge in AI/ML technologies and recent developments
* Admin-level familiarity with vSphere, RHV, Nutanix, or OpenStack

The Red Hat Hybrid Platforms Product Management team is looking for a Principal Product Manager (technical) to own and drive identity solutions in Red Hat OpenShift.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
In this role, you are responsible for how people, workloads, and software agents authenticate to OpenShift and how OpenShift decides what they are allowed to do. You will work with the Engineering and Product teams who build and deliver those capabilities. The product area includes:
  
  

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will contribute to company strategy and work closely with Engineering, Marketing, Support, Sales, Security, and Field teams.
  
  
You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.
  
  
As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

**What You Will Bring**

* 5+ years of enterprise software experience in product management, technical marketing, solutions engineering, or a similar technical product or customer-facing role
* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).
* Working knowledge of cloud workload identity. Depth in at least one of the following, and literacy in the others: AWS STS, Microsoft Entra workload identity, and Google Workload Identity or Workload Identity Federation
* A clear view of how a typical enterprise uses identity: single sign-on, group-based access, joiner-mover-leaver, non-human identities, and short-lived credentials as the default
* A clear view of how identity should work for agentic AI.
* Linux skills and direct experience with Linux containers and Kubernetes
* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions
* Ability to handle several competing priorities
* Bachelor's or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Willingness to travel up to 25%

**The Following Are Considered a Plus**

* Hands-on configuration of OpenShift identity providers, OAuth, external OpenID Connect, or cloud credential modes used by managed OpenShift
* Upstream participation in Kubernetes SIG Auth or a related CNCF project
* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory
* Understanding of zero trust principles.
* Experience with compliance programs in which identity is a control, such as FedRAMP or PCI
* Prior experience with agile delivery and with Jira or a similar tool

+ Demonstrated ability to collaborate on project timelines and maintaining project and technical documentation.
+ Experience working collaboratively across diverse teams and stakeholders.

+ Ability to meet stakeholder needs and carry-out expectations regarding project timelines, technical deliverables, and scope of work.

* User authentication and authorization, including the OpenShift OAuth server and external OpenID Connect integrations, Kubernetes RBAC, workload identity, multi-cluster authentication on OpenShift clusters
* Identity and user federation to secure agentic workflows in OpenShift.

You will plan and deliver product content for new releases and launches, prioritize and communicate requirements to guide development, support the field in advanced sales opportunities, perform competitive reviews, and work with partners. You will engage with the open source communities behind this work, including Kubernetes and other Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) projects.

As a Principal Product Manager, you need great communication, teamwork, and persuasion skills to articulate the product vision, align teams across the company, and influence stakeholders. This is an opportunity to work on a core platform control alongside some of the brightest minds in open source.

**What you will do:**
---------------------

* Collect input from OpenShift users, customers, community members, and internal stakeholders on how enterprises manage identity, and turn that input into strategy and a roadmap
* Define the product vision, the customer problems to solve, and measurable outcomes for authentication, authorization, and workload identity.
* Define and use metrics for adoption and measuring success
* Research commercial and do-it-yourself alternatives and use that research for competitive positioning
* Prioritize and document requirements, epics, and user stories, with acceptance criteria, for new releases
* Guide major enhancements with OpenShift Engineering, Kubernetes upstream, and adjacent product teams.
* Drive the identity model that agentic features in OpenShift and related products use, and work with those product teams so agents obtain authority through OpenShift identity and authorization
* Work with Sales on customer inquiries, presentations, and demos.
* Support go-to-market work, including presentations, blogs, demos, workshops, events, and sales enablement, and review documentation for this area
* Keep Engineering, Support, and Field aligned on direction, and own the translation of strategy into a release plan

**What you will bring:**
------------------------

* 5+ years of enterprise software experience in product management, technical marketing, solutions engineering, or a similar technical product or customer-facing role
* A track record of leading cross-functional work on a platform, security, or identity management, and of influencing people who do not report to you
* Direct experience with Kubernetes identity management.
* Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, and or how enterprises use identity provider (e.g. Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping Federate).
* Working knowledge of cloud workload identity. Depth in at least one of the following, and literacy in the others: AWS STS, Microsoft Entra workload identity, and Google Workload Identity or Workload Identity Federation
* A clear view of how a typical enterprise uses identity: single sign-on, group-based access, joiner-mover-leaver, non-human identities, and short-lived credentials as the default
* A clear view of how identity should work for agentic AI.
* Linux skills and direct experience with Linux containers and Kubernetes
* Working knowledge of the CNCF ecosystem and experience with open source projects
* Demonstrated ability to listen to customers, stakeholders, and engineering and turn that into product decisions
* Ability to handle several competing priorities
* Bachelor's or graduate degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience
* Excellent written and verbal communication
* Willingness to travel up to 25%

**The following are considered a plus:**
----------------------------------------

* Hands-on configuration of OpenShift identity providers, OAuth, external OpenID Connect, or cloud credential modes used by managed OpenShift
* Upstream participation in Kubernetes SIG Auth or a related CNCF project
* Experience with SPIFFE and SPIRE, LDAP, or Active Directory
* Understanding of zero trust principles.
* Experience with compliance programs in which identity is a control, such as FedRAMP or PCI
* Prior experience with agile delivery and with Jira or a similar tool
* A track record of enterprise product launches

You like making things run. You are the person who notices the spreadsheet that should be an automation, the report three people rebuild every month, and the field nobody fills in the same way twice. Operating as an autonomous, strategic thought partner to the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), this role is fueled by deep intellectual curiosity about the end-to-end operations of the business. The incumbent systematically looks into every corner of the commercial engine—evaluating top-line expansion, gross revenue retention (GRR), net revenue retention (NRR), and churn mitigation—to uncover non-obvious levers that drive step-change growth.
  
  
This position establishes segment-level performance clarity, sizes high-confidence growth and risk levers (Enterprise, SMB, Government), models unit economics, forecasts early-stage customer friction, and translates complex operational data into scalable business processes, targeted improvement initiatives, and measurable commercial results. Key Responsibilities & Time Allocation (100%)

* Identify, size, and economically model high-impact enterprise, SMB, and government growth opportunities (e.g., fleet migration pipeline mapping, camera green space capture rates) to guide go-to-market investments.
* Conduct econometric and sensitivity analyses on core revenue drivers (win rate, early-stage churn, NRR, pipeline velocity) across customer cohorts to maintain less than 5% revenue forecast variance per month.
* Model customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback, unit economics, and segment-specific margin contribution to provide executive leadership with financial framing for capital deployment, sales capacity, and incentive design.

GTM Process Optimization & Commercial Enablement (20%)

* Partner with Customer Success/Sales Enablement to operationalize competitive playbooks, objection-handling frameworks, and bundle packaging strategies across frontline sales cohorts.
* Evaluate and streamline GTM business workflows (e.g., lead routing, rep tiering structures) by operationalizing AI-driven frameworks and low-code automation to eliminate administrative drag and accelerate pipeline velocity.
* Monitor the ongoing adoption and financial ROI of deployed GTM programs, continuously refining enablement and sales motions to ensure sustained performance lift.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & GTM Alignment (35%)
  
  

* Strategic Revenue Liaison: Serve as the central strategic liaison between Sales Directors (Enterprise, SMB, Government), Finance, Product, and RevOps technical modelers to synchronize go-to-market strategies and eliminating silos and process breakdowns that cause revenue leakage.
* GTM Program Framework Architecture: Partner closely with pipeline and operations leads to architect program frameworks and Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) targeting parameters (e.g., account-tier thresholds, unit minimums, and deal-yield criteria) that direct frontline sales focus toward high-margin, high-retention opportunities.
* Executive Influence & Decision Alignment: Influence cross-functional leaders through objective data, qualitative narratives, and clear financial framing, driving consensus across the business on where to deploy capital, sales capacity, and operational effort.
* Joint GTM Strategy Orchestration: Co-lead the commercial operating cadence between Segment Strategy and GTM Operations, ensuring cross-functional handoffs between strategic insights, enablement rollout, and sales floor execution are seamless and measurable.

Executive Data Analysis, AI, & Predictive Reporting (15%)
  
  

* Oversee the deep extraction, econometric synthesis, and AI-accelerated modeling of complex segment data across Salesforce, Looker, and enterprise data warehouses to uncover leading indicators of churn, pipeline risk, or expansion upside.
* Transition fragmented, manual spreadsheets into unified, live executive dashboards (Airtable / Looker) that serve as the single source of truth for the ELT.
* Architect and leverage prompt-based AI frameworks, generative agents, and conversational intelligence tools to synthesize unstructured sales interaction data and competitor signals into real-time executive intelligence.
* Produce concise, qualitative executive narratives that explain why metrics are moving and define the specific operational actions required to accelerate performance.

* Act as a trusted strategic advisor to senior leadership by providing financial framing for accelerate/pause/stop decisions on portfolio programs and GTM bets.
* Mentor junior analysts and operations professionals, enforcing strict analytical rigor, data architecture standards, and peer-review quality control.

This is a new role within Full Bars, our in-house creative agency for Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile. The first priority in this role is to navigate — standing up new vendors, issuing PRs and POs, and tracking invoices to make sure vendors get paid on time — in partnership with Marketing, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and vendors themselves. This will be the main focus in the early part of the role before expanding into the rest of the team's operations. Beyond that, this person will audit the team's current SOPs and make recommendations on how to optimize and improve the way the team works and lead the evaluation of Airtable (or another PM platform) as a potential replacement for Wrike — building out the templates, workflows, and customizations if approved, and continuing to own and optimize that platform over time. Success means the Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile creative teams run on clear, well-managed processes — with strong visibility into capacity, and delivery for leadership.

**Responsibilities**:

* Set up and document the end-to-end vendor, procurement, legal, and AP process using T-Mobile's current systems — standing up new vendors, issuing PRs & POs, and tracking invoices to make sure they're paid on time — partnering closely with Marketing partners, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and vendors on resourcing, onboarding, and contract/work-order coordination.
* Create, own and send a weekly status update on all open POs, so stakeholders always know where things stand.
* Set up and maintain agency budget trackers to keep spend organized and visible.
* Audit the creative account teams' current SOPs and creative operations and make recommendations on how to optimize and improve them — then own that documentation going forward.
* Lead the evaluation of Airtable (or another platform) as a potential replacement for Wrike for the Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile creative teams and make a recommendation based on their needs.
* If a new platform is approved, build out all templates, workflows, and customizations from scratch, and roll them out to the Mint and Ultra teams.
* Own and continuously optimize the platform over time, adapting it as Mint Mobile and Ultra Mobile's needs change — this is an ongoing responsibility, not a one-time setup.
